newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close lower on dollar/Chicago.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close lower on dollar/Chicago.

text.p: Lower Chicago futures on the back of weekend rains in the U.S. Midwest, coupled with a drop in the dollar, led to easier asking prices at the close of the European vegetable oil market on Monday.
Traders reported little activity on a thin market.
"The holiday season will end soon and maybe currencies will settle down, but in the meantime all we can do is sit and wait," said a trader.
At the close of business Dutch soy oil sellers were 1.50 to 0.75 guilders down on a tradeless market.
Dutch/EU rape oil finished one to 1.25 guilders off after Nov/Jan fetched 105.50 guilders per 100 kg fob ex-mill.
In the palm oil sector only one trade was reported when Sept olein fetched $530 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
At the close crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged to $5 down while products were unchanged to $2.50 lower.
Lauric oils were neglected and finished with coconut oil $2.50 up while palmkernel oil was $7.50 higher to unchanged.
